subject: Logic
title: Why Fallacies Persuade
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why Fallacies Persuade.

hook.text: If fallacies are broken, why do millions of people fall for them every single day?

buildup.text: Our brains prefer speed over accuracy. Fallacies exploit mental shortcuts we rely on constantly.

discovery.text: Confirmation bias makes us accept bad arguments that support what we already believe.

twist.text: Skilled speakers wrap fallacies in emotion, authority, and confidence—making them nearly invisible.

climax.text: Fallacies persuade because they feel right. Logic demands we check whether they actually are.

quiz.question: Why do fallacies often persuade people?
